answer: Give every identity a shared-fate crew: agents join small groups whose rewards pool together, and if one member is caught faking work, the whole crew's pending payout is slashed. A Sybil attacker must then either run many separate crews — each needing real work history, like timber that only gains value after seasons of growth — or gamble everything on one crew where a single detection wipes out all its earnings. Honest crews police themselves because one bad relic of a member stains the velvet reputation they all share, so the cost of faking scales faster than the number of fake identities.
